newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Safeway cheery over Christmas.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Safeway cheery over Christmas.

text.p: British supermarket chain Safeway Plc continues to see a competitive food retail market but hopes that Christmas trading will be higher, chief executive Colin Smith told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"I am positive about Christmas, there are some good statistics on retail generally...(and) I would hope that (consumers) would have more confidence to spend," he said.

Safeway said sales from existing stores rose five percent in the first five weeks of the second half after a gain of 5.1 percent in the first half, as pretax profits edged up seven percent to 228.2 million stg.
Smith said he hoped a petrol price war, which took 10 million stg off profitability of forecourts in the first half, would not impact in the second half.
"I would hope that would be the case," he said.
He said sales per square foot were running at 14.63 stg in the first half and the company's target of 15 stg per square foot was "clearly in reach within the next two years."
Smith said the company aimed to increase sales by "continuing to focus on the family shopper...being competitive on price, providing great food and great customer service.
But he added that the group was "in a very competitive sector and margins at the moment are slightly down."
Increased efficiencies would mean that the company could reinvest in competitiveness, Smith said.

He said the results showed the company was delivering on the promises made when its Safeway 2000 strategic review was completed in the summer and was on track to deliver 60 million stg of savings outlined at that time.
He added that the group was "picking up pace" with innovations, advertising and new products.

Safeway has introduced self-scanning, where customers track and total their own shopping as they move round the store and avoid checkout queues, to 100 stores where it accounts for 20 percent of sales.
It plans to use it in a further 50 stores next year, Smith said.
"It is ahead of where I expected it to be in such a short time," he added.
